findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The ice machine baffle and inner surfaces were observed to have soil accumulation. The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and instructed to clean the baffle as well as the inner surfaces and maintain the ice machine free of soil buildup. Ensure the ice machine baffle and inner surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will follow up on March 9, 2026 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Strawberry fruit jam labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” was observed on a shelf. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed as well as educated and the jam was voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” are kept in the cooler and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in all the coolers. The PIC was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Soil and debris accumulations were observed on the dish holder by the three-compartment sink.
2. Debris accumulation was observed in the utensils holder under the dish holder by the three-compartment sink.

The PIC was instructed to have those surfaces clean. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 The facility has a routine for making and using small batches of boba. The boba still needs to have a time as a control marking of some sort. Discussed using a white board or the tile back splash. The boba on the counter top did not have a time as control tag. Make sure to mark in use boba with 4 hour time tag and use or discard any left after the 4 hours. Boba was marked.

(A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11:The counter top edge piece to the right of the hand sink on the line is no longer sealed to the counter top. Caulk seal behind the prep sink on the make line area is molded. Remove the seal, clean and replace.

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) No certified food protection manager (CFPM) on duty at time of inspection. Employees are food handler certified. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all operational hours. There are three certified food protection manager’s licensed; however, there is infrequency with how often the CFPM’s are at the facility. During today’s inspection, the main manager/owner who is a CFPM was stated to be gone until the weekend due to being out of town. Provided class list to encourage taking the course and exam. Another CFPM should be licensed to have enough to cover being present during operational hours. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 7/22/19, 6/30/20, 10/27/21, and 9/20/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

Observed all ice cream time controlled utensils to be rinsed in the handsink. Wash, rinse, sanitize in 3 compartment sink every 4 hours. Not taking place. Do not used handsink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

Observed both employees to dump ice cream tong water in handsink and rinse tongs. There is a language barrier. Attempted to explain handsink is for handwashing only. COS. Items need to be washed, rinsed, sanitized in 3 compartment sink. Observed PIC to dampen and ring in-use rag in handsink. Handsink is for handwashing ONLY.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no certified food protection manager on duty. Employees were food handler certified. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all operational hours. There are two certified food protection manager’s licensed; however, there is infrequency with how often the CFPM’s are at the facility. During today’s inspection, the main manager/owner who is a CFPM was stated to be gone until the weekend due to being out of town. Provided paperwork for taking the course and exam. Another CFPM should be licensed to have enough to cover being present during operational hours. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 7/22/19, 6/30/20, and 10/27/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed no hand washing before engaging in food behaviors. Inspector witnessed both employees to not wash hands prior to starting to make drinks. Discussed with all staff during inspection. Ensure appropriate hand washing before food engagement - soap, hot water, paper towels to dry hands. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off the faucets in order to not cross contamination hands. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/20/20 and 10/27/21.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sanitization bucket to be too low - 100 ppm of quat. Sanitizer concentration should be 200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonium. Facility has test strips and Inspector noted one employee actively testing the, “sanitize”, basin of the 3 compartment sink. Ensure frequent changes of the sani bucket to maintain 200-400 ppm of sanitizer. Discussed with employees. COS.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 

Observed a set of tongs within a water with basin on top of the cold holding of the rolled ice cream machine. Inspector probed one employee about the process utilized regarding the tongs and water. Employee stated they change the water several times a day and rinse off the tongs. It is correct to be changing the water several times a day (every 4 hours), but the tongs and basin should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours as well or replaced by new tongs and basin (food contact surface). A policy has been created with SCDPH in the past for ice cream utensils (see attachment in CDP). Historically, this facility was utilizing time control, then changed to putting ice cream utensils inside the top prep cooler near the rolled ice cream machines. It appears the time control policy is being utilized again. Ensure a time stamp system for every 4 hours to wash, rinse, sanitize and that all staff is aware of this operational procedure. Inspector will follow-up on 9/30/22.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed several coolers not to have thermometers within. Most coolers at the facility have an outside digital thermometer, but no internal thermometer. Ensure all coolers have a thermometer within to measure the temperature of the cold holding unit.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Observed the 3 compartment sink to have a constant drink despite pressing back on both faucet handles. A minor leak appears to be dripping below the 3 compartment sink. Ensure repairs are made to the triple sink.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed all the cabinets in the ice cream prep area to have exposed/bare wood. Seal with paint or clear coat. Ensure the cabinet bases and smooth and easily cleanable. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no CFPM present during inspection. PIC is food handler’s licensed. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all hours of operation. The facility has 2 certified food protection manager’s that are licensed; however, these CFPM’s are not frequently at the facility. Ensure 1-2 more CFPM’s are licensed before the next routine inspection. Provided paperwork for taking the classes. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/30/20 and 7/22/19.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements during inspection. Provided new copy. Ensure this document is reviewed and all employee’s sign a copy. Keep within a public health folder or binder. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/30/20.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed PIC to done gloves before engaging in food prep and not wash hands before donning gloves. Inspector stopped PIC and kindly asked to wash hands. Education was provided regarding appropriate hand washing techniques. Discussed turning off faucet with a barrier such as a paper towel. Ensure hand washing is performed before donning gloves and returning to food preparation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/30/20.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple areas of facility where in-use rags were present and not in a sanitization bucket with solution. Discussed changing practices with PIC. When rags are not in-use, they should be within the sanitization bucket with accurate concentration of sanitizer. A new sani bucket was made and rags were placed within the bucket. Cease practice of leaving in-use rags on counters. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/30/20 and 7/22/19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

(REPEAT) Observed no functioning sanitization bucket during inspection. Facility is just placing in-use rags within an empty bucket. Cease practice. Provided education on proper sanitization bucket procedure and in-use rag procedures (see violation #41). Quat - 200 ppm. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/30/20.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

Observed in-use rags not being stored in sanitizer throughout facility. Sani bucket was made and rags immersed. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

Observed no sani bucket present. Bucket was made. Tested at 200 ppm. COS. 

Discussed sani bucket is needed during all hours of operation. In-use rags must be in sanitizer at all times when not being used.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed facility to not have a CFPM present when inspector's arrived. Please ensure there is a CFPM during all hours of operation. Provided paperwork for PIC. CFPM arrived during the inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed employee to wash gloves in hand sink and attempt to return to food service. Employee's must discard gloves between uses and practice appropriate hand washing before donning new gloves. Discussed with employee COS.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.12 (C) Single-Use Articles stored in an unapproved location. Single-Use Articles may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. Reference 4-903.12.

Observed single-use utensils to be stored at PIC's home. All items related to business should be within the permitted facility. Please ensure that single-use utensils or any other facility item remains at the permitted location.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed facility to lack CFPM during inspection. Only one CFPM is available at facility. Discussed with PIC that there must be one CFPM present during all hours of operation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

Observed facility to lack signed employee health reporting agreements nor do employee's understand prevention of transmission of foodborne disease. Exclusion and restriction paperwork provided during last inspection was posted on back prep wall (along with Norovirus illness clean-up policy). All food handler's must sign the employee health reporting agreement and be explained significance of document. Inspector will follow-up on 7/9/20.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed multiple employee's to change gloves without washing hands between tasks. Discussed the need to wash hands with proper technique between changing gloves and task use. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.
(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 
(C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed hand sink to be blocked by ice cubes in ziplock bag. Inspector removed bag to wash hands. Hand sinks must be free and accessible for employee's to wash hands at all times. COS.

(REPEAT) 6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. Reference 6-301.11

Observed no liquid soap in both facility hand sinks. Soap was replaced for inspector to wash hands. Discussed need for hand sinks to be stocked with paper towels, soap, hot water, and a trash recepticle at all times. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Crepe spatula and ice cream scoop (food contact surface) is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed crepe spatula and ice cream scoop to be stored in water. PIC indicated that spatula and container of water are cleaned nightly. Food contact surfaces must be washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every 4 hours. Discussed this procedure with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

After discussion with PIC, the prep items near the ice cream cart/crepe area are being washed and rinsed near the prep sink in this area, but not being sanitized until the end of the night. Food contact items should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours. Discussed with PIC and food handler's that 3 compartments sink should be utilized throughout the day to wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact utensils and surfaces. Inspector will spot check in future.

(REPEAT) 4-702.11  (P) Observed employee clean ice cream scoop and use it without sanitizing. After cleaning, utensils must be sanitized before use. Reference 4-702.11.

Observed employee to take in-use ice cream scoop stored in water and empty container, rinsed, and re-fill, then return to service without cleaning and sanitizing scoop between uses. Discussed need to wash, rinse, and sanitized between uses or every 4 hours. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items throughout facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple food items to lack date marking throughout facility:
1. Crepe batter in two prep coolers.
2. Ice cream base (mixed) in three prep coolers.
3. Opened milk in two prep coolers.

Food items should be date marked and discarded within 7 days. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated items had been made or opened within 48 hours. Inspector will follow-up to check routine date marking on 7/9/20.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

Observed food storage containers to be not labeled in multiple areas of facility. Items included sugar, flour, taro, coffee, and milk powder. Common names should be written on outside storage bin. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed multiple areas of facility where in-use rags were present and not in a sanitization solution. Discussed need for sanitization bucket to be present during hours of operation (and frequently changed), as well as in-use rags being stored in this sanitization bucket at all times. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed in-use spatula's and ice cream scoop to be stored in water on ice cream cart and crepe prep area. PIC indicated water and spatula's are changed nightly or as needed. Spatula's, ice cream scoops, and containers should be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours (see violation #16). No tracking system to monitor cleaning of spatula and ice cream scoop (food contact surfaces). Spatula and ice cream scoop may be stored in running water, in container of hot water maintained at or above 135 degrees F, or on a clean and sanitized surface. Created a Time as a Public Health Control policy for facility. This was discussed during last routine inspection. See attached. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of inside cabinents are no longer easily cleanable. Replace with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

Observed interior of all base cabinents to have unsealed particle board on the bottom. Paint or seal these surfaces so they are non-absorbant and easily cleanable. Discussed repairs with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availablity (Pf)

Observed facility to lack any sanitization bucket during inspection. In-use rags were being stored on counter. Discussed need for a sanitization with correct concentration to be present during all hours of operation. In-use rags must be stored in sanitization buckets. Prepared bucket with PIC. Bucket registered at 200 ppm. COS.

(REPEAT) 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility to lack test strips for quaternary ammonium. Discussed need for test strips at facility. Inspector will follow-up on 7/9/20. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on milk tea sealing machine. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed large accumulation of soil residue and debris on milk tea sealing machine. PIC indicated machine is cleaning once a week. Inspector suggested every other day due to build-up on debris. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

Observed facility to lack food handler's licenses for all employee's. Employee's must have a food handler's card within 30 days of employement. Discussed providing copies at facility. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/22/19.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: The person in charge at the time of the inspection has not completed the Certified Food Protection Manager course yet and there is no one on site with this certification at the time of the inspection. The person in charge at the time of the inspection must have this certification. 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment: There are employee beverages located all over the facility--above food prep areas in both the front and the back, next to the clean cups for customers at the front counter, on the prep table in back near the reach in freezer. Some with lids and straws and others without. Store all personal beverages with lids and straws in an area below or away from food and food prep areas as discussed. 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking in the food preparation area. Provide designated area for drinking.  Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Soap and paper towels were not available at the front hand washing sink. The back hand sink only had hand sanitizer in the dispenser and a bar soap. Hand washing sinks do not have signage identifying them as such and employees were observed using the hand washing sink in the front as a rinse sink for containers. Hand washing sinks are fod hand washing only and should be labeled as such and stocked will a supply of warm water, liquid soap and paper towels at all times. Liquid soap and paper towels were provided during the inspection and hand washing signs were left with the facility. 6-301.14  (C) A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. Reference 6-301.14.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11  (Pf) Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink. Provide liquid soap at hand washing sink. Reference 6-301.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1) Observed in use spatulas stored in water with the container of water being emptied, rinsed, re-filled and returned to service without cleaning and sanitizing spatulas in between use. 2) Measuring cups for ice cream (which contains heavy cream) are not being washed, rinsed and sanitized between use and are stored at room temperature. They are only being rinsed in the prep sink. Provide enough cups so that they may be washed, rinsed and sanitized in between use or discuss using a time as a control with a written policy.  4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A). 4-602.11 (C) (P) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11  (P) After cleaning, utensils must be sanitized before use. Reference 4-702.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: 1) Milk in a cooler with ice at the bottom only was probed at 54F from the top of the container (that was not in contact with ice). 2) Ice cream bases, which contain heavy cream were observed stored on the counter top at room temperature (chocolate probed at 55F). All items containing milk, egg or other TCS foods must be maintained at 41F or below at all times. Items out of temperature were discarded. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed crepe mix, cheesecake portioned in refrigeration, and open gallons of milk that were not marked with the date of opening or preparation. Date mark all of these items and hold no longer than 7 days maximum. 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Wet wiping cloths for the front of the house (ice cream slabs) are reported to just be water and observed wet on the counter in between use. Sanitizer solution was prepared during the inspection and cloths were moved to be stored in this solution. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: 1) Observed ice scoop handle stored in contact with ice and ice bin not covered at the front. Keep handle extended up and out of the ice at all times and keep ice bin covered. 2) In use spatulas are stored in water on ice cream carts. PIC states water is changed after every 3 customers but this is not being tracked in any manner. Store spatulas clean and dry in between use and wash, rinse, and sanitize at least every 4 hours. 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Inside cabinets appear to be unsealed particle board on the bottom. Paint or seal these surfaces so the are non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 4-101.19  (C) Paint or seal to provide corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: PIC is not able to locate test strips for quaternary ammonium sanitizer. Provide test strips for testing the concentration of quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution. 4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The milk tea sealing machine is observed soiled. Clean this machine as often as necessary. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: No food handler certificates are available at the time of the inspection. All food handlers must successfully complete an ANSI approved food handler training program (approximately 1 hour long and can complete entirely online).
